name: Can I keep my bathtub and still make the bathroom accessible?

mainEntity.name: Is it possible to remodel for accessibility without removing the tub in a family bathroom?
mainEntity.text: Is it possible to remodel for accessibility without removing the tub in a family bathroom?

acceptedAnswer.text: A bathtub can stay in the design if the bathroom must serve children, guests, or multiple users, but it will limit accessibility compared with a walk-in or curbless shower. A tub transfer bench, handheld shower head, and well-placed grab bars can make tub use safer for some people. However, the high step-over edge remains a challenge for wheelchair users, people with balance issues, and anyone recovering from surgery. If accessibility is the primary goal, replacing the tub with a barrier-free shower usually gives better long-term value. In homes where a tub must remain, the remodel should still improve access around it by widening the approach, adding non-slip flooring, and making sure controls are easy to reach from outside the basin. The best decision depends on who uses the bathroom most often and whether universal access or family flexibility matters more.
acceptedAnswer.description: Yes, but a traditional tub is one of the biggest barriers to accessibility. Keeping it usually means adding a tub transfer bench, improving floor clearance, and using grab bars, but it will not be as accessible as replacing the tub with a shower.
